title: Why Gold Is In a Structural Bull Market
excerpt: A trader's view on what's actually driving gold beyond the headlines — and what would change my mind.
author: Waqar Ahmad
authorBio: 10+ years trading forex & gold markets. Opinions are personal, not financial advice.
body:
This is my own read on gold heading into the second half of 2026 — not a prediction with a guaranteed outcome, just the reasoning I'm actually trading around. Markets can and do prove any single view wrong.

## Central bank demand hasn't slowed down

Central banks globally have kept accumulating gold reserves at a pace well above the decade average, largely as a hedge against currency and geopolitical risk. That's structural buying, not speculative flow — it doesn't disappear on a bad CPI print.

## Real yields matter more than headlines

Gold's biggest moves tend to track real (inflation-adjusted) interest rates more closely than the nominal headlines suggest. When real yields compress, gold tends to find support even amid short-term dollar strength.

## What would change my mind

A sustained, aggressive rise in real yields, a genuine and lasting reduction in central bank buying, or a major de-escalation in the geopolitical risks currently supporting safe-haven demand — any of these would meaningfully shift this view.

This is a personal opinion piece reflecting my view at the time of writing, not financial advice. Markets are dynamic, and I may be wrong.
